name: Bodh Gaya
summary: The holiest place in Buddhism: the Buddha attained enlightenment here under the Bodhi tree, and the Mahabodhi Temple now stands beside a descendant of that tree. Monasteries built by Buddhist nations from Bhutan to Japan ring the town, and the ruins of Nalanda university and the hills of Rajgir make a full-day trip.
seasonNote: October to March is cool and dry; December and January bring Tibetan pilgrims, prayer festivals and sometimes teachings by the Dalai Lama. April to June is very hot.
arrival: Gaya airport (15 minutes away) has flights from Delhi and Kolkata and seasonal flights from Southeast Asia. Gaya Junction station is 30 minutes away, with trains from Delhi, Varanasi and Kolkata.
gettingAround: The town is small and walkable; e-rickshaws link the temples and monasteries. Hire a car for Nalanda and Rajgir.
cashTip: Carry cash; cards work only in bigger hotels. UPI is common.
foodTip: Monastery guesthouses and Tibetan cafés serve thukpa and momos; try Bihar's litti chokha, roasted wheat balls with mashed aubergine.
buyTip: Prayer beads, singing bowls, Buddha statues and Tibetan textiles from the market by the temple.
baseArea: Hotels and monastery guesthouses within walking distance of the Mahabodhi Temple

connections.note: Train from Gaya Junction; about 6 hours by road.

items.name: Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi Tree
items.summary: The 50 m brick temple marking the spot of the Buddha's enlightenment, with the sacred Bodhi tree and the Vajrasana diamond throne behind it.
items.expect: Shoes off at the gate; phones are not allowed inside (use the lockers); open to all.
items.tip: Come at dawn or dusk to sit among monks chanting under the tree.
items.why: The holiest place in the Buddhist world and a World Heritage Site.
flow: Leave phone and shoes at the gate.
Walk the circuit, then sit under the Bodhi tree.

items.name: Great Buddha Statue
items.summary: A 25 m stone Buddha seated in meditation, consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 1989.
items.expect: A short walk from the main temple, set in gardens.
items.tip: Pair it with the monasteries on the same road.
items.why: Bodh Gaya's best-known landmark after the temple.

items.name: International monasteries
items.summary: Temples built by Thailand, Bhutan, Japan, Tibet, Myanmar and others, each in its own national style.
items.expect: Most close at midday; remove shoes and dress modestly.
items.tip: See the Thai temple's golden roofs and the Royal Bhutan Monastery's painted walls.
items.why: A tour of Buddhist Asia in one small town.
flow: Walk on to the Bhutanese and Japanese temples.

items.name: Dungeshwari Cave Temples
items.summary: Cave shrines where the Buddha is said to have fasted for six years before going to Bodh Gaya.
items.expect: A short climb; small Tibetan monastery at the top.
items.tip: Go in the morning with a rickshaw; children may beg, so give to the monastery instead.
items.why: The story of the Buddha's path before enlightenment.

items.name: Nalanda ruins
items.summary: The red-brick ruins of one of the world's first great universities, where thousands studied from the 5th to the 12th century.
items.expect: A large site with a museum; little shade.
items.tip: Combine with Rajgir's Vulture Peak in one day trip.
items.why: A World Heritage Site and a cornerstone of Buddhist learning.

items.name: Vulture Peak, Rajgir
items.summary: The rocky hilltop where the Buddha gave many teachings, reached by a ropeway near the Peace Pagoda.
items.expect: Steps and a chairlift.
items.tip: Go late afternoon on the way back from Nalanda.
items.why: One of the main sites of the Buddha's life.

items.name: Tibetan cafés
items.summary: Simple cafés serving thukpa noodle soup, momos and butter tea, busiest in pilgrim season.
items.expect: Many open only from October to March.
items.tip: Try the vegetable momos with chilli sauce.
items.why: The comfort food of the pilgrims.
flow: Walk the lanes by the temple.

items.name: Litti chokha stalls
items.summary: Bihar's signature dish: roasted wheat balls stuffed with spiced gram flour, with smoky aubergine chokha.
items.expect: Street stalls, best in the evening.
items.tip: Ask for extra ghee on the litti.
items.why: The taste of Bihar.
flow: Find a stall roasting over coals.

items.name: Monastery guesthouse meals
items.summary: Several monasteries serve simple vegetarian meals to visitors and guests.
items.expect: Fixed meal times; donations welcome.
items.tip: Ask at your guesthouse which monastery kitchens are open to visitors.
items.why: A quiet meal in the spirit of the place.

name: Udaipur
tagline: Rajasthan's city of lakes and palaces
summary: Udaipur's white palaces rise from the shores of Lake Pichola, with an island palace floating in the middle. The old city is a tangle of havelis, temples and rooftop restaurants, and the hill forts of Kumbhalgarh are a day's trip away.
seasonNote: October to March is ideal; the lakes are fullest just after the monsoon. Summer is hot; the monsoon (July to September) is green and quiet.
arrival: Udaipur airport is 30 minutes from the old city, with flights from Delhi and Mumbai. Trains run from Jaipur and Delhi.
gettingAround: Walk the old city lanes; rickshaws and taxis for further sights.
cashTip: UPI and cards are common; carry cash for boats and small shops.
foodTip: Rajasthani thalis with dal baati churma, gatte ki sabzi and laal maas, best eaten on a lakeside rooftop at sunset.
buyTip: Miniature paintings, silver jewellery, block-printed textiles and leather from the old-city lanes.
baseArea: The old city near Lal Ghat and Gangaur Ghat, or Hanuman Ghat across the lake

items.name: City Palace
items.summary: A vast lakeside palace complex built over 400 years, with mirror halls, courtyards and views over Lake Pichola.
items.expect: Busy at midday; allow two to three hours.
items.tip: Go at opening time and take the audio guide.
items.why: The grandest palace in Rajasthan.
flow: Museum rooms, then the lake terraces.

items.name: Lake Pichola boat ride
items.summary: A boat across the lake past the Lake Palace hotel to the island palace of Jag Mandir.
items.expect: Boats leave from the City Palace jetty.
items.tip: Take the sunset boat for the palaces in golden light.
items.why: The defining view of Udaipur.
flow: Board at the City Palace jetty.

items.name: Jagdish Temple
items.summary: A 17th-century Vishnu temple covered in carvings, just above the City Palace.
items.expect: Steep steps; shoes off; busy at evening aarti.
items.tip: Visit at the evening aarti.
items.why: The old city's main temple.

items.name: Bagore Ki Haveli dance show
items.summary: An 18th-century haveli museum with a nightly show of Rajasthani folk dance and puppets.
items.expect: Show at 7pm; queue early.
items.tip: Arrive 30 minutes early for a good seat.
items.why: The liveliest evening in the old city.

items.name: Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh)
items.summary: A hilltop palace with sweeping views over the lakes and the Aravalli hills.
items.expect: Taxi or shuttle to the top.
items.tip: Go for sunset.
items.why: The best sunset in Udaipur.

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
items.summary: A 15th-century hill fort whose walls run for 36 km, among the longest in the world.
items.expect: About 2.5 hours each way; combine with the Ranakpur Jain temple.
items.tip: Leave early and see Ranakpur's marble temple on the way.
items.why: A World Heritage hill fort.

items.name: Ambrai
items.summary: A lakeside terrace facing the City Palace, lit up at night.
items.expect: Book ahead for a table on the water.
items.tip: Reserve for sunset and order laal maas.
items.why: The best view in Udaipur with dinner.

items.name: Natraj Dining Hall
items.summary: An unlimited vegetarian Rajasthani thali, refilled until you stop them.
items.expect: Busy and fast.
items.tip: Pace yourself; the refills keep coming.
items.why: A classic Rajasthani thali.

items.name: Old-city rooftop cafés
items.summary: Rooftop restaurants above Lal Ghat looking over the lake and palaces.
items.expect: Relaxed; many screen the film Octopussy, shot here.
items.tip: Pick one facing the City Palace at sunset.
items.why: The quintessential Udaipur evening.

name: Jodhpur
tagline: The blue city under Mehrangarh Fort
summary: Jodhpur's old city is painted in shades of blue and crowded beneath the cliffs of Mehrangarh, one of India's most impressive forts. Spice markets ring the clock tower, and the edge of the Thar Desert begins just beyond town.
seasonNote: October to March is best; the Rajasthan International Folk Festival is at Mehrangarh in October. April to June passes 40°C.
arrival: Jodhpur airport is 20 minutes from the old city with flights from Delhi and Mumbai; trains from Jaipur take about 5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the blue lanes; rickshaws for the fort and Umaid Bhawan.
cashTip: Carry cash for the lanes and markets; UPI is common.
foodTip: Mirchi vada and kachori from the clock tower stalls, makhaniya lassi, and laal maas.
buyTip: Spices and tea from Sardar Market, bandhani tie-dye, and jodhpurs from the tailors.
baseArea: Heritage guesthouses in the blue old city below the fort

items.name: Mehrangarh Fort
items.summary: A towering 15th-century fort on a cliff, with carved palaces, a superb museum and views over the blue city.
items.expect: Steep ramps; a lift is available; allow three hours.
items.tip: The audio guide is excellent; stay for sunset on the ramparts.
items.why: One of the finest forts in India.

items.name: Jaswant Thada
items.summary: A white marble memorial to Maharaja Jaswant Singh II, with a lake and fort views.
items.expect: Calm, small, a short walk from the fort.
items.tip: Visit right after Mehrangarh.
items.why: A peaceful marble jewel.

items.name: Blue City lanes
items.summary: Lanes of blue-washed houses below the fort, with temples, stepwells and rooftop views.
items.expect: Narrow, hilly lanes; motorbikes squeeze through.
items.tip: Visit Toorji Ka Jhalra stepwell on the way.
items.why: The picture of Jodhpur.
flow: Wander downhill to the clock tower.

items.name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
items.summary: A huge Art Deco palace finished in 1943, now part hotel, part royal residence and part museum.
items.expect: Only the museum is open to non-guests.
items.tip: See the vintage car collection.
items.why: One of the last great palaces built in India.

items.name: Clock Tower and Sardar Market
items.summary: The busy bazaar around the old clock tower, selling spices, textiles and bangles.
items.expect: Crowded and chaotic.
items.tip: Climb a rooftop nearby for the view of the fort above.
items.why: The commercial heart of the old city.

items.name: Rao Jodha Desert Rock Park
items.summary: A restored desert landscape of volcanic rock with native plants and trails under the fort walls.
items.expect: Little shade; trails of up to two hours.
items.tip: Walk at sunrise or late afternoon.
items.why: A different, wild view of Mehrangarh.

items.name: Mirchi vada at the clock tower
items.summary: Big green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter.
items.expect: Hot from the fryer; spicy.
items.tip: Pair it with a pyaaz kachori.
items.why: Jodhpur's famous snack.

items.name: Makhaniya lassi stalls
items.summary: Thick saffron lassi topped with butter cream, a Jodhpur speciality.
items.expect: Small shops; mornings and afternoons.
items.tip: Ask for the saffron makhaniya lassi.
items.why: The city's sweet signature.
flow: Find a lassi shop by the clock tower.

items.name: Blue City rooftops
items.summary: Guesthouse rooftop restaurants with fort views, serving Rajasthani curries.
items.expect: Relaxed; the fort is lit at night.
items.tip: Order laal maas, a fiery mutton curry.
items.why: Dinner under the floodlit fort.
flow: Dinner as the fort lights up.

name: Kochi · Kerala
tagline: Spice port, fishing nets and the Kerala backwaters
summary: Kochi's Fort Kochi quarter blends Portuguese, Dutch, British and Jewish history with spice warehouses, art cafés and the giant Chinese fishing nets. It is the gateway to Kerala's backwaters, where houseboats drift through palm-lined canals.
seasonNote: November to March is dry and warm. The southwest monsoon (June to September) is heavy but lush, and good for Ayurvedic treatments. The Kochi-Muziris Biennale art festival runs from December every other year.
arrival: Cochin International Airport is about an hour from Fort Kochi; trains arrive at Ernakulam.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle Fort Kochi; ferries cross to Ernakulam; the metro covers the mainland.
cashTip: UPI and cards are common; carry some cash for ferries and stalls.
foodTip: Kerala fish curry, karimeen pearl-spot fried in banana leaf, appam with stew, and sadya feasts on banana leaves.
buyTip: Spices from Mattancherry's warehouses, Kerala tea, coir crafts and antiques on Jew Town Road.
baseArea: Fort Kochi heritage homestays and hotels

items.name: Chinese fishing nets
items.summary: Huge cantilevered fishing nets on the shore, lowered and raised by teams of fishermen.
items.expect: Busiest at sunset; fish stalls nearby.
items.tip: Fishermen may let you help pull the net for a tip.
items.why: The symbol of Kochi.

items.name: Mattancherry Palace
items.summary: A Portuguese-built palace given to the Raja of Kochi, famous for its Hindu mural paintings.
items.expect: Closed on Fridays; no photos inside.
items.tip: Pair it with the synagogue next door.
items.why: Some of India's finest temple murals.

items.name: Paradesi Synagogue and Jew Town
items.summary: A 1568 synagogue with hand-painted Chinese floor tiles, in a lane of spice and antique shops.
items.expect: Closed Fridays, Saturdays and Jewish holidays; shoes off.
items.tip: Browse the antique warehouses on Jew Town Road.
items.why: The oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth.

items.name: St Francis Church
items.summary: India's oldest European church, where Vasco da Gama was first buried in 1524.
items.expect: Small and simple.
items.tip: Walk on to Santa Cruz Basilica nearby.
items.why: A landmark of colonial history.

items.name: Kathakali performance
items.summary: Kerala's classical dance-drama, with elaborate make-up and costumes, staged nightly for visitors.
items.expect: Arrive early to watch the make-up being applied.
items.tip: Come an hour before the show for the make-up session.
items.why: The art form Kerala is known for.

items.name: Alleppey backwaters houseboat
items.summary: A day or overnight cruise on a rice-barge houseboat through Kerala's palm-lined canals and lakes.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours' drive; overnight boats include meals.
items.tip: Choose a smaller boat that can enter the narrow canals.
items.why: Kerala's signature experience.

items.name: Kashi Art Café
items.summary: A café and gallery in an old Dutch house, known for breakfasts and cakes.
items.expect: Garden seating; art on the walls.
items.tip: Come for breakfast and the chocolate cake.
items.why: The heart of Fort Kochi's art scene.

items.name: Fish stalls by the nets
items.summary: Buy fish straight from the stalls and have a nearby café cook it for you.
items.expect: Agree the cooking price first.
items.tip: Ask for tawa fry with Kerala masala.
items.why: The freshest seafood in Kochi.
flow: Take it to a cooking café.

items.name: Appam and stew breakfast
items.summary: Lacy rice pancakes with coconut milk stew, Kerala's classic breakfast.
items.expect: Served in small local restaurants in the morning.
items.tip: Try it with chicken or vegetable stew.
items.why: The Kerala breakfast.
